steps.message: Root cause found using the attempt 1 failure note. Working on branch codexray/repair-2.

sets.root_cause: delete_todo (app/routes.py:36-44) never checks the result of fetchone(). When the todo does not exist (or belongs to another user) row is None, Todo.from_row(None) raises TypeError, and Flask returns 500 instead of 404.

steps.message: Patched app/routes.py: delete_todo returns 404 when the todo is missing.

sets.diff:
--- a/app/routes.py
+++ b/app/routes.py
@@ -38,6 +38,8 @@ def delete_todo(todo_id):
     row = db.execute(
         "SELECT * FROM todos WHERE id = ? AND owner = ?", (todo_id, g.user)
     ).fetchone()
+    if row is None:
+        abort(404, description="todo not found")
     todo = Todo.from_row(row)
     db.execute("DELETE FROM todos WHERE id = ?", (todo.id,))
     db.commit()

steps.message: Independent review by deepseek-chat (patch author llama-3.3-70b-versatile was excluded): approve.

sets.reviewer_notes: The fix handles the missing row at the right place and also covers todos owned by other users, which now return 404 instead of 500. Minimal and safe. Optional follow-up: the same unchecked fetchone() pattern would affect any future single-todo endpoint, so a small helper like get_owned_todo_or_404 would prevent repeats.
